topology_reasoning_before_coding.device_identification: The black material forms a long, vertically symmetric, two-sided multi-rail coupler/MMI-like structure. Five narrow center rails run almost the full 120 um interaction length. Above and below them are mirrored access/comb structures: a broad slab-like access region near the center and a nested comb of five rails returning into thick side rails. The geometry is therefore best recreated as a primitive assembly of straight rails, broad slab sections, and smooth side-return paths rather than as a library device stencil.
topology_reasoning_before_coding.operating_interpretation: The five full-length center rails define the narrow coupling/interaction region. The upper and lower broad slabs act as access/multimode reservoirs, while the nested side-return rails control how fields are brought into or isolated from the central rail stack. Symmetry about y=0 is function-defining.
function_defining_knobs: transfer_length_um: horizontal length of the long interaction rails
rail_width_um: width of the narrow guide rails
rail_pitch_um: spacing of the central and comb rail stack
center_gap_um: gap between the two nearest central rails around the device midline
access_slab_height_um: height of the broad upper/lower access slabs
access_slab_length_um: straight length of the slab sections
side_rail_width_um: thickness of the side-return rails
side_taper_length_um: x/y extent of the side access transition
trim_delta_length_um: verifier knob that lengthens one real rail by one rail width per micron

iterations.change_made: Initial primitives-only parametric script using measured rail centers, scan-derived slab slices, comb rail rectangles, and extruded side-return paths. Stopped because IoU exceeded 0.85; residual diff is dominated by thin rail edge offsets and slightly over-wide side-return strokes.
Metadata/top-level-cell write fix only: wrote the GDS with metadata disabled so spec_optimization layer-area helpers see recreated_device as the top cell. Geometry and IoU unchanged.
